points.description: Enqueue happens at the end of the linked list: the rear of the queue points to the tail of the list, and new elements are added at the tail.
Dequeue happens at the beginning of the linked list: the front of the queue points to the head of the list, and elements are removed from the head.
Uses a linked list with both a front pointer (head) and a rear pointer (tail), so the queue works first-in-first-out.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying that enqueue is done at the tail (rear) and dequeue at the head (front) of the linked list, in any wording. Give part marks if only one end is correct, or if the idea is vague (for example, "add at one end, remove from the other" without saying which). Give no marks for the reversed assignment (enqueue at head, dequeue at tail) or for answers that describe a stack or an array.
